answer: The tide detector writes to sonnet, and jade makes public every merge. Submissions that land within 124 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. A farm scripting its whole fleet fires them together, which means the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 290 aliases out costs the operator real scheduling effort per key. That is 29 dollars per alias. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
